surfaces.part: stair plate with frame and descending step bands

answer.evidence: The whole 30px-wide sprite is a flat rectangular plate seen from above. A light frame runs along the top (row 1) and sides, and it encloses horizontal step bands. The bands run dark (rows 6-8), mid-grey (rows 14-19) and light (rows 21-28). The columns at x=9, 16 and 24 are identical on every row, so no part of the sprite changes with depth. Rows 28-29 narrow slightly to 28 and then 26 px wide, but this is only a corner trim of the frame. There is no vertical south face of 3 or more rows, no eave shadow under an edge line, and no ellipse. It reads as a flat floor decal, which matches the kind 'flat', and has no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small stair graphic: a light grey frame around dark horizontal bands with a few lighter step lines. It sits on a dark slate surround that reads as one flat fill. The measured 6 visible tones per tile is close to the paving reference (7) and above the grass (3), and measured flat coverage is 0%. By eye, though, the surfaces are flat bands with no stone speckle, grain or per-step shading like the cobbled paving reference, which shades each stone. Its dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline is a colourless black/grey line, where the grass reference has 0% neutral edges. That is the shallow sticker look. The paving reference is also mostly neutral (80%), but it has far richer surface texture. The candidate therefore looks thinner and flatter than the references, and with doubt the verdict is fail.

surfaces.part: stair opening: outer stone frame with a dark well and descending step bands

answer.evidence: The whole sprite is a 30px-wide plate that is 29 rows tall and has a nearly constant silhouette width (30 px from rows 1-27, narrowing to 28 and 26 only at the bottom corners). Inside, a light frame runs along the top row (row 1) and the sides. A dark well starts at rows 6-8 and gets lighter toward the bottom, with horizontal step bands. Light nosing lines at rows 21 and 25 each sit above a 2-3 row band. These are treads and risers of steps seen from above, not the front face of a standing body. The columns at x=9, 16 and 24 are identical, so there are no side faces or vertical structure. There is no standing volume and no south face of 3 or more rows, so this is a flat floor decal seen from above, which matches the kind flat.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate reads as a small stair icon (about 20x18 source px) framed in a neutral dark box on a flat slate backdrop, not a 4x3-tile ground patch, so it does not match the grass/paving references in kind or coverage. surfaces.part: descending stair treads and risers inside the dark pit

surfaces.part: stair-well plate: cream frame on the left and top, dark pit, and horizontal step bands descending into it

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a flat rectangle about 30 px wide and 29 rows tall, with a constant width of 30 from rows 1 to 27. The column scans at x=9, 16 and 24 are identical, so the drawing is made of uniform horizontal bands with no vertical variation across the width. Those bands are the cream frame (rows 1, 25), a dark pit (rows 6-16) and lighter step treads separated by darker risers (rows 9, 13, 17-24, 26-29). It is a plate seen from above, with no raised body, no front-edge line followed by eave shadow, and no ellipse. The few rows of light and dark at the bottom (rows 26-29) are step bands inside the frame, not a separate vertical south face. This matches the flat kind, so it is a flat top-down slab with no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small stair icon in a thick frame on a flat dark grey-blue backdrop, not a textured ground patch like the references.
